نَهِرٌ Much, (TA;) as also ↓ نَهيرٌ ; (K, TA;) both applied to water. (TA.) ―
-b2- A wide نَهْر [or river, or channel in which water runs]. (K.) ＝
-A2- رَخُلٌ نَهِرٌ A man of day-time; syn. صَاحِبُ نَهَارٍ; (S, K;) who makes inroads or incursions into the territories of enemies therein: (S:) or who works therein: (A:) a kind of rel. n.; as is shown by the ex. “لَسْتُ بِلَيْلِىٍّ وَلٰكِنِّى نهِرٌ
لَا أُدْلِجُ اللَّيْلَ وَلٰكِنْ أَبْتَكِرْ
” [I am not one of the night-time, but I am one of the day-time; I do not journey in the night, but I go forth early in the morning]: as though he said ↓ نَهَارِىّ . (Sb.) The verse is correctly related as above; not as it is given in the S. (IB.) ―
-b2- See also أَنْهَرُ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
